answer: Each identity must self-assess a price and pay a small Harberger tax on it every epoch, like a willow bending under a steady wind: anyone may buy the identity at its declared price, so a fake priced too low is bought and exposed, while a fake priced high pays a heavy tax per epoch. A sybil farmer with a thousand fakes pays the tax a thousand times over, each one perched on a narrow ledge between cheap exposure and costly upkeep. One honest agent pays a tiny tax on one jetty of identity and sails on, while cloning multiplies the bill, not the power.
